P0299 · low boost / loss of power
engine mesin turbo underboost boost tenaga hilang lemah power asap smoke hose selang

P0299 reports an underboost condition; it does not prove a failed turbocharger. Reduced power, air leaks, unusual turbo noise or smoke may accompany it. Preserve the original code text, status, module and freeze-frame/load conditions before clearing anything. Other codes may change the diagnostic order.

Stop load testing for heavy smoke, rapidly falling oil level, oil-pressure warning, abnormal mechanical noise, overheating or uncontrolled engine speed. Stop safely and arrange qualified assistance. Let the engine and exhaust cool before inspection. Keep hands/tools clear of rotating parts; never run with intake plumbing removed. No road test when safe control or drivability is doubtful.

Lamp, camera, protective equipment and the exact engine repair manual. A compatible scanner may supply original DTCs and requested/actual boost, RPM and load. A regulated leak tester or actuator test equipment requires the manufacturer procedure and limits; this guide supplies no test pressure.

1. Verify the engine is turbocharged and confirm code/module from the original report. If identification or code definition is uncertain, stop at reference gathering. If correct, continue to 2.

2. With engine stopped and cool, inspect accessible air filter, intake/charge hoses, joints and intercooler for restriction, loose joints or visible damage. If a defect is found, photograph and follow the exact manual repair, then verify. If none, continue to 3. Oil staining alone does not prove a leak.

3. A qualified technician checks for charge-air leaks using the vehicle procedure. Leak confirmed → repair that leak and retest; no leak → continue to 4. No valid pressure limit/procedure → defer this test.

4. Compare requested/actual boost only at manufacturer-defined safe conditions; check absolute versus gauge units and sensor plausibility. Implausible readings → follow sensor/circuit diagnosis. Real low boost → investigate control/vacuum/actuator, exhaust restriction, fueling and lubrication in the manual diagnostic order. Inconclusive → record results and refer, not replace the turbo by code alone.

General turbo-engine triage; no boost target, leak-test pressure, actuator travel, preload, torque or sensor threshold is supplied. Garrett is a general system source. GM PI1366 concerns only its listed 1.4 L LUJ/LUV applications; its wastegate repair is not a rule for other vehicles. A P0299 topic match is not a vehicle/manual match.

Repair a proven hose/joint/filter defect only using specified parts and tightening/installation instructions. Actuator, sensor, turbo or exhaust replacement requires evidence from the exact manual tests. Do not adjust wastegate preload, bypass emissions controls or install a turbo solely because P0299 exists. Correct any proven lubrication/contamination cause before replacing a damaged turbo.

Record repaired defect, parts, manual reference and measurements. Reinspect connections/leaks, then repeat the original complaint conditions only if safe and permitted by the manual. Compare requested/actual readings to the correct specifications and rescan the relevant modules. Preserve before/after codes; clear only under the repair procedure with permission. Recurring symptoms/codes or incomplete test conditions → unresolved, not confirmed repaired.
Engine overheating / temperature warning
engine mesin panas overheat overheating temperature suhu coolant radiator steam uap

Temperature warning/message, temperature gauge outside its normal range, steam or coolant loss. A normal or missing generic DTC does not rule out overheating. Record the exact dashboard message, operating conditions and coolant-loss history.

Stop safely for an overtemperature warning, steam, major coolant leak or loss of power; do not keep driving to reproduce it. Follow the vehicle operator emergency instructions and arrange recovery if unresolved. Do not open a hot or pressurized cooling-system cap, touch hot parts, or approach escaping steam. Electric fans can start unexpectedly. No universal cool-down time is safe for every vehicle.

Protective equipment, lamp, camera and exact coolant/cooling-system manual. A compatible scanner can record temperature but a sensor value is not proof of actual coolant condition. Pressure tester, thermometer or electrical tests require trained use and the specific test points/limits.

1. Record warning and stop conditions. Steam/major leak or repeated warning → no running test; refer/recover. Otherwise wait until fully cold under the vehicle instructions, then 2.

2. With engine off and cold, visually check accessible reservoir level against its vehicle markings and look for external leak traces without dismantling. Low level/leak → identify and repair the cause via the manual before running. Level appears correct → 3; it does not prove normal circulation.

3. Check repair history for wrong coolant, recent opening/air entry or recurring loss. Suspected issue → qualified technician follows specified fill/bleed and leak diagnosis; no such evidence → 4. Never mix coolant by color alone.

4. A qualified technician follows the exact fan, thermostat, pump, pressure and temperature-sensor diagnostic sequence. Confirmed failed test → conditional repair. Missing limits or no fault found → record observations, stop and refer; do not assume a head gasket or thermostat failure.

No universal normal temperature, fan-on threshold, pressure, coolant chemistry/mix, cap opening time or bleeding procedure is provided. Ford owner information supports warning/cap precautions only for its stated application, not a cooling-system repair manual for this vehicle. Hybrid/high-voltage cooling circuits need their own trained procedure.

Only repair a confirmed leak or failed component using the matching manual, approved coolant, torque and fill/bleed process. Do not add stop-leak or substitute an unverified coolant. Internal engine repair requires specific diagnostic evidence. If the manual or safe equipment is missing, refer without running an overheating engine.

After the specified cold-fill/bleed procedure, verify level/leaks, temperature and fan behavior against the exact manual under safe stationary conditions. Stop immediately if the warning returns. Recheck cold level as directed and document before/after observations and codes. A temporarily extinguished lamp or no codes alone does not establish a successful repair.
SRS / airbag warning
srs airbag restraint sabuk belt pretensioner lampu warning peringatan keselamatan

SRS/airbag warning remaining on, returning, or not following the vehicle specified self-check. The system may not protect occupants as intended. Passenger-airbag status indications are not automatically SRS faults; distinguish them using the exact operator manual. SRS codes and definitions are manufacturer/module specific.

Do NOT activate/deploy an airbag or pretensioner, perform output tests, or apply voltage to any initiator. Do NOT use a multimeter, ohmmeter, test lamp, jumper or substitute resistor on squib/initiator circuits. Do not probe, unplug, repair or disturb SRS connectors/components from this general guide. No generic battery-disconnect waiting time is supplied: energy isolation and waiting periods must come from the exact manufacturer procedure and trained personnel. Crash/deployment, damaged wiring or water exposure → stop work and refer to an SRS specialist.

Original compatible SRS scanner report, camera, exact SRS repair manual, VIN and qualified SRS technician. A generic engine OBD reader or this guide cannot establish SRS access or system health. Any special manufacturer test equipment is for the qualified technician under the exact manual, not general probing.

1. From outside the components, record warning behavior and compare with the operator manual self-check. Missing manual → leave applicability unverified and refer. Abnormal behavior → 2.

2. Ask about crashes, deployed restraints, water ingress and recent seat/steering/battery work. Any crash/deployment/water or visible damage → no disturbance; specialist assessment. Otherwise → 3.

3. Obtain a report from equipment explicitly compatible with this SRS module. Record scanner model, exact module, full DTC/subcode, status and timestamp. No communication or no SRS-capable tool → record not tested, not no fault. Valid report → 4.

4. Match VIN/module/manual and follow only the qualified technician diagnostic path. Circuit-related code does not itself identify a failed airbag, clock spring or ECU. No exact procedure → stop at evidence collection; no electrical or connector work.

No exact SRS manual is matched. Isolation method, stored-energy wait, connector locks, test adapters, wiring, replacement and calibration depend on VIN/system. Aston Martin OTH-01-1043 applies to listed legacy models; Toyota 23TA08 is a specific recall with VIN/part eligibility. Neither authorizes those repairs on this service vehicle.

Only a qualified SRS technician may repair a demonstrated fault under the matching manufacturer instructions, including isolation, approved parts and post-crash replacement rules. No emulator, bypass, warning-lamp suppression or crash-data reset as a substitute for repair. Do not replace an airbag or module on a generic code interpretation. Missing evidence/manual → refer.

The qualified technician checks installation and required initialization/calibration, warning self-check and all relevant SRS DTCs using the matching procedure. Preserve before/after reports and unresolved findings. Do not test protection by activating restraints. Warning off or no generic engine codes alone does not prove SRS readiness; safety release requires the vehicle procedure and responsible technician.
Transmission warning / shift problems
transmission transmisi gearbox shift perpindahan gigi slip slipping hentakan warning peringatan

Transmission warning, delayed/harsh engagement, unexpected gear behavior or slipping. Record exact message, gear, cold/hot condition, load, recent work and full TCM report. An engine emissions code list may not include transmission-specific faults.

Stop safely for overheating/stop messages, loss of drive, uncontrolled movement, heavy leak, burning smell or severe noise. Secure the vehicle using its operator instructions; arrange recovery if safe operation is doubtful. No stall test, improvised pressure test, forced shift, repeated slipping road test or adaptation reset from this guide. Keep clear of hot fluid and moving driveline; never work beneath an unsupported vehicle.

Exact transmission identification and repair manual, original compatible TCM scanner report, camera and qualified technician. Fluid-level tools, lifting equipment or pressure gauges require the exact safe procedure. A generic OBD link is not a guarantee of TCM coverage.

1. Record stop messages and movement control. Unsafe/overheated → stop, follow operator instructions and recover; do not reproduce. Safe stationary inspection → 2.

2. Identify transmission type/code and history, including fluid used and previous repairs. Unknown type → collect reference before service. Correct identity → 3.

3. Visually document accessible leak traces without opening plugs or touching hot parts. Leak found → qualified diagnosis; do not top up by guess. No visible leak → 4; absence of a leak is not proof of correct fluid level.

4. Obtain exact TCM DTC/subcode/status and compatible live data. No communication → not tested, refer for coverage/power/network diagnosis using the manual. Data available → use exact manual sequence to distinguish electrical/control, fluid and mechanical causes. Inconclusive → no component replacement or reset.

No universal fluid type, capacity, checking temperature, pressure, torque, adaptation or reset values exist here. AT/CVT/DCT/manual procedures differ. Ford owner sources illustrate warning handling and application-specific fluid checks, not a matched repair manual. Do not copy their numerical values to another transmission.

Repair only a verified leak, electrical fault or component failure using the exact transmission procedure and approved fluid/parts. Do not flush, add additives, change solenoids, reset adaptations or replace a gearbox solely from symptoms/codes. Adaptation or programming is allowed only when explicitly required by the matching repair procedure and qualified equipment.

Qualified technician verifies fluid level under specified conditions, leak freedom, required initialization and relevant TCM data/codes. A controlled engagement/road check is only permitted after safety is established and under the manufacturer procedure. Document before/after complaint behavior and readings. Persistent slip, warning or incomplete test → unresolved, not repaired.
Unknown code / unsupported module — safe evidence collection
unknown unsupported umum tidak dikenal code kode abs body other

No specific procedure is available for an unknown code/module or unexplained symptom. This is a general fallback, not a code definition. Manufacturer-specific codes and subcodes require the exact module documentation. No codes, an empty report or a failed connection cannot establish that no fault exists.

Do not continue driving/testing with brake or steering impairment, overtemperature, oil-pressure warning, fuel leak, uncontrolled movement or restraint damage. Stop safely and refer/recover. Do not probe SRS initiators, command actuators, touch high-voltage systems, bypass safety devices or clear evidence to silence a warning.

Camera, original scanner report, exact vehicle/module identity and operator/repair documentation. Verify scanner/interface protocol and voltage ratings before connecting; no unverified truck/24 V support is implied. Specialist-compatible equipment is needed for systems not covered by generic engine OBD.

1. Record the symptom and exact warning. A stop condition → secure vehicle and seek specialist assistance; otherwise → 2.

2. Preserve scanner manufacturer/model, module, full code/subcode, status, timestamp and report/photo. Missing/unreadable report → record not tested and request a valid report; never infer no fault. Valid evidence → 3.

3. Confirm VIN, year, engine, transmission and market. Obtain the applicable code definition and repair-manual revision. No match → remain unverified and refer; exact match → 4.

4. A qualified technician follows that manual diagnostic tree, recording test conditions, measured values and specified limits. Failed test → only its supported repair; ambiguous/pass-with-symptom → continue that diagnostic tree or escalate, not automatic confirmation.

No verified vehicle specification or code-specific repair is supplied. Operator manuals explain warnings; workshop repair manuals define diagnostic tests and limits. A search hit, generic code description or another vehicle bulletin does not establish applicability. Record actual references and measured results in the service diagnosis record separately.

Do not recommend or perform a part replacement, ECU reset, coding, adaptation or code clearing without a matched procedure and supporting evidence. With confirmed identity, manual and failed tests, the qualified technician may perform the procedure-specific repair. Otherwise leave diagnosis unconfirmed and refer.

Use the matched manual verification procedure after an evidenced repair, compare before/after measurements and reproduce the complaint only when safe. Preserve unresolved codes and untested systems. No codes alone never means all-clear. Without applicable reference or completed verification, record unresolved/unverified.
